meta.title: alpaka kernels for matrix multiplication and addition
meta.body_summary: Add an example demonstrating matrix multiplication and addition using cuBLAS with alpaka, as an initial step toward multi-backend integration for performance-critical operations.

perf_labels.notes: OpenAI_Codex-assisted example for matrix operations with cuBLAS; maintainers request multi-backend support and merging with existing example; PR remains open with design discussion.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 380 changed lines (mostly in a new example file), this is a small-sized addition. As an incremental example addition, it is not merged yet due to extensive design feedback and expectation to demonstrate multi-backend integration.

review_details.concern_detail: Maintainers suggest moving the example into existing useBLASInAlpaka directory and extending it to support CUDA, HIP, and CPU backends via preprocessor guards and a unified API, rather than a standalone CUDA-only example. CI also fails due to missing cublas_v2.h (known CI bug).
review_details.performance_claim: Using cuBLAS for matrix multiplication and addition can accelerate compute-bound operations on GPUs.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The PR demonstrates a need for multi-backend performance evidence and architectural integration with existing examples; the agent's initial scope (CUDA-only) falls short of maintainers' expectations for a library integration example.

detection_detail.code_reading: mehmetyusufoglu questioned the kernel summing logic (single-thread vs parallel). Others reviewed the overall approach and suggested merging with existing BLAS example.
detection_detail.ci_auto: CI failures due to missing cublas_v2.h prompted discussion about CI environment bugs.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: The example can be built locally with CUDA, but CI cannot compile due to missing cublas; multi-backend reproducibility not demonstrated.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No regression issue; CI failures are attributed to known environment problems, not code regression.

core_change_summary.description: Added new example 'matrixMulAdd' under example directory. The first commit provided a basic matrix multiplication and sum using alpaka kernels; the second commit integrated cuBLAS for the matrix multiplication step, demonstrating a chained GEMM operation with timing.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Top-level CMakeLists.txt adds the new example subdirectory.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: Added new example with alpaka-only matrix multiplication and sum.
Second commit: Replaced alpaka matrix multiplication with cuBLAS call, added timing measurements, and updated CMake for CUDA dependencies.

review_signals.summary: Suggested extending the example to support CUDA, HIP, and CPU backends using preprocessor guards and possibly merging with existing BLAS example.
review_signals.action_taken: Author agreed and is planning to work on it.

review_signals.summary: Proposed a template-based API design that dispatches to cuBLAS or a generic alpaka kernel depending on the accelerator type.
Provided step-by-step suggestions: move to useBLASInAlpaka, add implementations for each backend, merge them with if defined, and wrap into a generic function.
Asked why the kernel sums all four elements with only one thread, questioning the parallelism.
review_signals.action_taken: Author acknowledged the observation in a reply comment.

collaboration_trajectory: OpenAI_Codex-assisted PR opened with a basic matrix multiply-add example.
Within hours, maintainers suggested expanding to multi-backend and merging with existing BLAS example.
Author agreed and discussed use case for SOFIE.
CI failure due to missing cublas prompted discussion on environment fix.
Maintainer provided step-by-step suggestions for extending the example.
No additional commits after feedback; PR remains open.
